construction_markdown:
This is a foundation handoff, not a duplicate leaderboard submission. The strongest independently accepted construction in the durable corpus is as follows.

Fix `p(Z)=Z^16+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1`, `E=F_2[Z]/(p)`, and `alpha=Z mod p`. Let `A=span_{F_2}{1,alpha,...,alpha^14}` and `Y=F_2^15`, both in binary coefficient order. For `z=sum_{i=0}^{15} z_i alpha^i`, define `H(z)_y=z_0+sum_{i=1}^{15}z_i y_i`. For every `f in E[X]` of degree at most 64, set `C(f)_(a,y)=H(f(a))_y` for `(a,y) in A×Y`.

This gives the exact `[2^30,1040,535822336]_2` RS–affine code. The message hyperplane on which the coefficient of `1` in the constant coefficient of `f` vanishes gives a 1039-dimensional two-sided `1/512`-biased core, and the full code is that core direct-summed with the all-one word.

The new reusable landscape result is an exact correction and ceiling for homogeneous AGHP/Walsh descent. Over `F=F_{2^15}`, the words `c_P(x,y)=Tr(yP(x))`, `deg P<=64`, form an exact `[2^30,975,535822336]_2` balanced core. Since every such word vanishes at `y=0` and has weight at most `n/2`, adjoining the all-one word safely gives `[2^30,976,535822336]_2`. Moreover, 976 is the maximum after this single augmentation throughout the exact complete homogeneous-Walsh architecture with a `q`-linear outer code of length `L<=q` and `Lq=2^30`.

The target forces `d_o>=ceil(511L/512)`, so Singleton gives `t<=floor(L/512)+1`. Hence the balanced-core dimension is at most `m(floor(L/512)+1)` and the standard all-one augmentation is at most 976, uniquely as a parameter optimum at `a=m=15`. Degree-64 RS evaluation attains core 975 and augmented 976. The campaign ledger should distinguish these two numbers.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Intended recipients: trace/BCH researcher and bottleneck breaker. In the full odd-degree trace space, dropping the constant row cannot exploit the one-sided target. For any nonzero `f(x)=Tr(P(x))` with `f(0)=0`, choose `t` with `f(t)=1`; after trace-reducing even exponents, `g(x)=f(x+t)+f(t)` remains in the same odd-degree space and satisfies `S(g)=-S(f)`. Thus a one-sided signed-sum certificate for the whole space is automatically two-sided. Beating 1040 through degree 69 therefore needs a genuine uniform improvement from the generic `68 sqrt(q)` bound to `64 sqrt(q)`, not sign selection.

The affine truth-table blocks `b_0+<b',y>` would then give a deterministic `[2^30,1041,>=535822336]_2` code. distance_audit: `D=(1/2-2^-10)2^30=2^29-2^20=535822336`; equivalently the permitted one-sided signed sum is `n-2D=2^21`, while two-sided small-bias parameter is `tau=2^-9=1/512`.
For the RS–affine code, `wt(C(f))=2^14(32768-N_0(f)+N_1(f))`. If `f` is nonconstant, both `N_0(f)` and `N_1(f)` are at most 64.
The constant cases are exhaustive: `f=0` is zero, `f=1` is all-one, and every other nonzero constant gives weight `2^29`. Thus every nonzero word has weight at least `D`.

Exact distance is witnessed by a degree-64 polynomial with 64 prescribed roots, scaled by the least nonzero field element that avoids value `1` on every nonroot. At most 32,704 of 65,535 scales are forbidden, and the resulting weight is `32704*16384=D`.
The 1039-dimensional RS–affine hyperplane has all nonzero weights in `[D,n-D]`; complementation therefore preserves its distance when the all-one word is adjoined.
For homogeneous AGHP, a polynomial with `r` roots has exact weight `(32768-r)16384`. The root bound gives `r<=64`, and a product of 64 distinct linear factors attains `D`.
No conditional inner code, sampled object, or asymptotic estimate contributes to the reported dimension or distance.
explicitness_audit: The degree-16 field polynomial and polynomial basis are fixed; its Rabin irreducibility certificate is reproduced in the accepted durable construction.
Rows are indexed by `(j,i)` with `0<=j<=64` and `0<=i<=15`; columns are the explicitly ordered pairs `(a,y) in A×F_2^15`.
Every generator entry is obtained directly from bounded degree-16 field arithmetic and a 15-bit affine dot product. No matrix search, lookup table, randomness, puncturing, or padding is used.

The full matrix has exactly `1040n` output bits. The stated nested loops run in fixed-parameter `O(n)` time, with all dependence on 1040 rows, degree 64, and field degree 16 displayed in the runtime bound.

The least-scale choice used only for the exact-distance witness can be found by scanning 65,535 explicitly ordered field elements, which is polynomial in `n`; it is not part of the generator definition.
The homogeneous 976-dimensional comparator and the 991-dimensional trace comparator likewise have direct monomial/trace row enumerators running in fixed-parameter output-linear time.
This landscape-scout turn made no publication claim or file edits. Consequently the data validator and dashboard build were not run; those belong to a writable integrator step.

generator_matrix.algorithm: Use `E=F_2[Z]/(Z^16+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1)` and `alpha=Z mod p`. Enumerate rows lexicographically as `(j,i) in {0,...,64}×{0,...,15}` and columns as `(a,y) in A×F_2^15`, where `A=span{1,alpha,...,alpha^14}` and both factors use binary-integer order. For each entry compute `z=alpha^i a^j mod p`, extract `z=sum_{r=0}^{15}z_r alpha^r`, and output `z_0+sum_{r=1}^{15}z_r y_r`. The resulting row is exactly `C(alpha^i X^j)`, so all 1040 rows and all `n` columns are emitted.
generator_matrix.runtime_bound: At most `1040*n*(64*O(16^2)+O(15))` bit operations and `O(log n)` counter space; hence fixed-parameter `O(n)` time, with output size `1040n`.
generator_matrix.runtime_proof: Computing one entry from scratch uses at most 64 multiplications of degree-16 binary field elements, one bounded reduction modulo the fixed polynomial per multiplication, coefficient extraction, and a 15-bit dot product. There are exactly `1040n` entries. Schoolbook field multiplication costs `O(16^2)` bit operations, so the displayed bound follows and is `n^{O(1)}`. The algorithm streams entries and does not invoke any search or oracle.

proof_markdown:
### 1. Target normalization

For a binary word `c`, put `S(c)=sum_j (-1)^{c_j}=n-2 wt(c)`. Thus `wt(c)>=D` is exactly the one-sided condition `S(c)<=2^21`. A two-sided small-bias proof uses the stronger condition `|S(c)|<=2^21`, or normalized bias `tau=2^-9`; the campaign distance gap itself is `2^-10`.

### 2. Strongest durable endpoint

Use the accepted Rabin certificate for `p(Z)=Z^16+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1`. Evaluation and `H` are binary-linear. If `C(f)=0`, injectivity of `H` makes `f` vanish on all 32,768 points of `A`; since `deg f<=64`, this forces `f=0`. Therefore `dim C=65*16=1040`, while `|A×Y|=2^30`.

For `N_i(f)=|{a in A:f(a)=i}|`, the inner weights are zero for symbol 0, 32,768 for symbol 1, and 16,384 for every other nonzero symbol. Hence

`wt(C(f))=2^14(32768-N_0(f)+N_1(f))`.

If `f` is nonconstant, both `f` and `f-1` have at most 64 roots, so `N_0,N_1<=64` and the weight lies in `[D,n-D]`. Nonzero constants other than 1 are balanced, while `f=1` is all-one. This proves the distance lower bound for every nonzero word. To attain it, take a polynomial `g` with 64 fixed distinct roots in `A`. For a nonroot `a`, at most one nonzero scalar `mu` makes `mu g(a)=1`; fewer than 65,535 scales are therefore forbidden. The first allowed scale gives `N_0=64,N_1=0` and weight exactly `D`.

Imposing one binary equation on the constant coefficient and choosing it to exclude `f=1` produces a 1039-dimensional core whose nonzero weights all lie in `[D,n-D]`. Adding the all-one direction complements those words, proving the stated decomposition.

### 3. Exact homogeneous-Walsh ceiling

Let `q=2^m`, let the outer length be `L=2^a`, and assume `Lq=2^30` and `L<=q`. Concatenate a `q`-linear `[L,t,d_o]_q` outer code with the complete homogeneous Walsh map, under which zero has weight zero and every nonzero symbol has weight `q/2`. The binary dimension is `mt` and distance is `qd_o/2`. Meeting the target requires

`d_o>=ceil(511L/512)`.

Singleton gives

`t<=L-d_o+1<=floor(L/512)+1`.

Since `m=30-a` and `a<=m`, one has `a<=15`. For `a<9`, the outer distance must equal `L`, so the augmented dimension is at most 31. For `a=9,...,15`, the augmented bounds are respectively `43,61,96,163,290,529,976`. Thus 976 is the unique parameter maximum, at `a=m=15`; this is not a uniqueness claim for the code and does not cover affine or punctured inner maps.

At `a=m=15`, take the degree-at-most-64 Reed–Solomon evaluation code. For `P!=0` with `r(P)` roots, homogeneous character orthogonality gives

`S(c_P)=2^15 r(P)` and `wt(c_P)=(32768-r(P))16384`.

The root bound gives exact core parameters `[2^30,975,D]_2`, with equality from 64 linear factors. Every core word has weight at most `n/2` and vanishes at every `y=0` coordinate, so the all-one word is independent and its coset consists of complements of weight at least `n/2`. This proves the exact augmented `[2^30,976,D]_2` endpoint. The safety of this augmentation uses the homogeneous nonnegative-bias property; it is not valid for an arbitrary merely one-sided code.

### 4. Trace comparator and sign symmetry

Over `F_{2^30}`, the functions

`b+Tr(sum_{j=1,3,...,65} a_j x^j)`

form a 991-dimensional code. For a nonzero polynomial of odd degree `d<=65`, the Artin–Schreier/Hasse–Weil estimate gives `|S|<=(d-1)2^15<=2^21`. The strict inequality `2^21<2^30` also rules out a nonzero evaluation kernel, so the balanced core has dimension `33*30=990`, and the constant direction yields 991.

This generic certificate is sharp in scope: odd degrees through `2t-1` give dimension `30t+1` and allowance `2(t-1)2^15`, hence `t<=33`. Moreover, the one-sided condition gives no extra room for the full odd-degree space. If a nonzero trace function `f` satisfies `f(0)=0`, choose `u` with `f(u)=1`. Translation followed by repeated use of `Tr(a x^(2r))=Tr(a^(2^29)x^r)` puts `g(x)=f(x+u)+f(u)` back in the same odd-exponent function space, and `S(g)=-S(f)`. Thus every allowed signed sum is paired with its negative.

### 5. Complete-output classical amplification

For the literal fresh-seed implementation in Naor–Naor, the first base family has distinguishing probability `1/8`. Useful expander contraction makes the paper's threshold `alpha_G<1/4`, so the independent-product stage needs at least 11 samples; rank at least 32 already forces at least `32^11>2^30` starting seeds. In the alternative code-based branch, any fitting case with `K>=813` must have base relative distance at most one half by Plotkin. The independent stage then needs at least three base samples, and the fresh coefficient stage contributes at least two choices. Hence the literal enumerated support has at least `2K^3`; because `2*813^3=1,074,735,594>2^30`, this scoped implementation has `K<=812`. Compressed equivalent distributions and redesigned correlated samplers are not excluded.

The newer durable finite audits similarly close only their stated complete-cloud certificates: direct Ta-Shma output is capped at augmented dimension 65, ordinary one-edge mixing at 946, and uniformly repeated complete Cartesian XOR powers at 1025. Sparse, nonuniform, or directly one-sided path families need new proofs.

### 6. Handoff conclusion

The strongest complete explicit small-bias object in the current corpus is therefore the 1039-dimensional RS–affine balanced core, whose all-one augmentation gives the exact target code of dimension 1040. The new homogeneous ceiling fixes the AGHP accounting at `975+1=976`, while translation symmetry closes the apparent one-sided loophole in the full odd trace family. None of these scoped results is a global upper bound on binary linear codes.
